source: Zhang et al. (2018), AJ 155, 83, 'Phase Curves of WASP-33b and HD 149026b and a New Correlation between Phase Curve Offset and Irradiation Temperature' (doi:10.3847/1538-3881/aaa458; arXiv:1710.07642). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of WASP-33b, 11 April 2012. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of best-fit parameters (table:all_results), column WASP-33b 4.5 um, and the table of dayside and nightside brightness temperatures (table:toy_model). The model is a first-order sinusoid, L_p = C + c1 cos(2 pi t/P) + c2 sin(2 pi t/P); the table prints its amplitude, sqrt(c1^2 + c2^2), and its phase offset, "with a negative offset meaning the maximum occurs before the center of the eclipse", which is a hot spot east of noon. The star pulsates (a delta Scuti variable); the fit models the pulsations with a Gaussian process.

eclipseDepth.cell: 4250 +/- 160 ppm, "the planetary flux at the center of eclipse divided by the stellar flux"

model.equation: L_p = C + c1 cos(2 pi t/P) + c2 sin(2 pi t/P), printed as its amplitude sqrt(c1^2 + c2^2) and its phase offset from the eclipse centre.

offsetDegreesEast.cell: -19.8 +/- 3.0 degrees: negative, so the maximum comes before the centre of the eclipse and the hot spot lies 19.8 degrees east

nightsideK.where: table:toy_model, WASP-33b 4.5, T_b,night (from F_p - 2 A cos(phi))
